sentences.text: 4. According to the prosecution, respondent No.2 lodged an FIR alleging inter alia that marriage of respondent No.2 was solemnized with applicant- Shivam Choudhary in accordance with Hindu rites and rituals on 12.07.2021.
Her husband is posted as Constable in SAF, 17th Battalion and now he is at Raisen.
In the marriage, her elder paternal uncle and aunt (Tau and Tai) and mother had given Rs.25 lacs cash, house-hold articles and gold jwellery, as per their capacity.

After marriage, when she went to her matrimonial home, Shivam Choudhary (husband), Bharat Kumar Choudhary @
Chhutaiya (father-in-law), Smt. Suneeta @ Guddi (mother-in-law), Nishant Choudhary @ Krishna (younger brother-in-law) and Ku. Kamini Choudhary @ Pooja (sister-in-law) taunted her that her family members have cheated them and asked to bring Rs.10 lacs from her family members, else they would not keep her.
She tried to appease them by saying that her father is no more and her elder paternal uncle (Tau) and mother are incapable of giving such amount.
When she came to her parental home and narrated the entire episode to her mother Poonam Dubey, elder paternal uncle (Tau)- Harishankar Sharma, elder paternal aunt (Tai)-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:10924 Mithlesh Sharma and elder sister- Priyanka,
then her family members made her to understand that she has been recently married and with passage of time everything would be alright.

On 15.08.2022, when she was in her matrimonial house, Bharat Kumar Choudhary @ Chhutaiya (father-in-law), Smt. Suneeta @ Guddi (mother-in-law), Nishant Choudhary @ Krishna (younger brother-in- law) and Ku. Kamini Choudhary @ Pooja (sister-in-law) demanded additional dowry by hurling abuses.
When she asked not to abuse then they assaulted her by kicks and fists and kept the entire Stridhan with them.
Thereafter, they left her to her parental home.
On 06.09.2023, when she and her family members went to her matrimonial house and her family members tried to have a talk as regards the said incident, on which her in-laws started abusing.
Then, they came back to the parental home.
Thereafter, she submitted an application before the Mahila Paramarsh Kendra, Bhind where compromise took place between them and she started living with her husband at Raisen.
On 23.03.2023, her husband started hurling abuses.
When she objected to it, her husband assaulted her with kicks and fists.

On being narrated the incident, her elder paternal uncle and aunt (Tau and Tai)
reached to bring her.
When she was going to her parental home, he threatened her for dire consequences, if the matter is reported to Police.

When he objected to it, then Aashish @ Aashu broke his mobile Samsung M-12 and also assaulted him by fist and blows.

It also appears that a complaint was made by respondent No.2 to Superintendent of Police, Bhind and accordingly, an enquiry was conducted and ultimately the husband of respondent No.2 as well as respondent No.2 agreed to resolve all their disputes and husband of respondent No.2 also agreed to keep his wife along with him.
Thus, it is clear that respondent No.2 was constantly making complaints with regard to physical and mental cruelty meted out to her.
It is not out of place to mention here that Shivam Choudhary is a police constable and is posted at Company 17 th Battalion, Special Police Force, Bhind.

He lodged the report at Police Station Raisen in Crime No.112/2023 alleging that he was beaten by Harishankar (Tau of respondent No.2) and Aashish @ Aashu (cousin of respondent No.2) and his mobile was also broken.
In the FIR itself, it is mentioned that cousin of respondent No.2 too had threatened that applicant has to keep his sister/respondent No.2 as per her wishes, otherwise he would be killed.

Although the correctness of FIR in Crime No.112/2023 is not in question but one thing is clear that incident took place on account of some dispute related to behaviour of in-laws with respondent No.2.
The allegations are specific and therefore, this Court is of considered opinion that no case is made out warranting interference.
9. Accordingly, M.Cr.C. No.30792 of 2023 filed by Shivam Choudhary is hereby dismissed.

Furthermore,
the marriage was performed on 12.07.2021 and FIR was lodged on 17.05.2023, thus, the FIR is delayed and therefore sought quashment of FIR on the aforesaid two grounds.
11. Per contra, the application is vehemently opposed by counsel for the State as well as counsel for respondent No.2.

The allegations made in the FIR have already been reproduced.
14. Thus, the FIR can be bifurcated in two parts.

The first part speaks about the cruelty meted out to her by applicants till 15.08.2022 i.e., when she was ousted by applicants from her matrimonial house and again on 06.09.2023 when respondent No.2 was abused by applicants when she tried to come back to her matrimonial house.
The second part of the FIR is concerning the allegations against Shivam Choudhary (husband of respondent No.2).

Therefore, this Court is not concerned with the incident which took place after the matter was compromised in the Police counselling but this Court is concerned about the allegations which were made prior to 15.08.2022 and on 06.09.2023.

The marriage was performed on 12.07.2021 and according to the prosecution case,

sentences.text: Respondent NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:10924 No.2 had already lost her father and her marriage was performed by her Tau, mother and other relatives.
On 15.08.2022, she was ousted by applicants after abusing and beating her by fist and blows.
Turning a married woman out of her matrimonial house by itself is a cruelty.
This incident of ouster took place on 15.08.2022 whereas the FIR was lodged on 17.05.2023 i.e. about nine months after the incident.
Thereafter, once again when respondent No.2 tried to come back to her matrimonial house, then again she was maltreated by applicants.
The FIR was lodged by respondent No.2 by making a written complaint on 17.05.2023.

In the FIR, it is alleged that on 06.09.2023,
when she tried to go back to her matrimonial house, then she was abused and maltreated whereas written complaint was made on 17.05.2023, therefore, date 06.09.2023 appears to be a typing error in the written complaint.
15.
Be that whatever it may be.
16. Even for the purposes of delay, if we ignore the date 06.09.2023, then it is clear that at least on 15.08.2022, respondent No.2 was ousted on account of non-fulfillment of demand of dowry.

17. The Supreme Court in the case of Rupali Devi v. State of U.P., reported in (2019) 5 SCC 384 has held as under:-
"14.

entities.text: Rupali Devi v. State of U.P., reported in (2019) 5 SCC 384
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "Cruelty" which is the crux of the offence under Section 498-A IPC is defined in Black's Law Dictionary to mean "the intentional and malicious infliction of mental or physical suffering on a living creature, esp. a human; abusive treatment; outrage (abuse, inhuman treatment, indignity)".
Cruelty can be both physical or mental cruelty.

The impact on the mental health of the wife by overt acts on the part of the husband or his relatives; the mental stress and trauma NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:10924 of being driven away from the matrimonial home and her helplessness to go back to the same home for fear of being ill-treated are aspects that cannot be ignored while understanding the meaning of the expression "cruelty"
appearing in Section 498-A of the Penal Code.

The emotional distress or psychological effect on the wife, if not the physical injury, is bound to continue to traumatise the wife even after she leaves the matrimonial home and takes shelter at the parental home.

Even if the acts of physical cruelty committed in the matrimonial house may have ceased and such acts do not occur at the parental home, there can be no doubt that the mental trauma and the psychological distress caused by the acts of the husband including verbal exchanges, if any, that had compelled the wife to leave the matrimonial home and take shelter with her parents would continue to persist at the parental home.

Mental cruelty borne out of physical cruelty or abusive and humiliating verbal exchanges would continue in the parental home even though there may not be any overt act of physical cruelty at such place."
18.

This Court in the case of Amar Singh vs. Smt. Vimla decided on 22.06.2021 in Criminal Revision No.2376/2020 (Gwalior Bench) has held that compelling a married woman to live in her parental Shivam Choudhari vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60158594/
5 home amounts to cruelty.
19. Thus, it is clear that ouster of a married woman on account of non- fulfillment of demand of dowry by itself is a continuous offence and it amounts to mental cruelty.

The period of limitation for taking cognizance for offence under Section 498A of IPC is three years from the date of last incident provided NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:10924 it is not continuous one.
The marriage itself was performed on 12.07.2021 and the FIR was lodged on 17.05.2023.
By no stretch of imagination it can be said that any incident of cruelty was barred by time.
Furthermore, act of ouster amounts to continuous mental cruelty.

20. So far as the prosecution of near and dear relatives of husband is concerned, it is well established principle of law that general and omnibus allegations are not sufficient to compel the near and dear relatives of husband to face the ordeal of trial.
The allegations must be clear and specific.
The husband of respondent No.2 was posted in Bhind or Raisen whereas applicants are the residents of Itawah.
From the compromise which was arrived at during the police counselling, it is clear that respondent No.2 was left by her husband in her matrimonial house i.e. at Itawah.
Even in the first part of the FIR, all the allegation have been specifically made against applicants.
The allegation of ouster after beating and abusing her is also against applicants.
As already held, ousting a married woman on account of non-fulfillment of demand of dowry by itself amounts to mental cruelty.
Not only the FIR is not barred by time as per the provisions of Section 468 of Cr.P.C. but even otherwise, the FIR cannot be quashed on the ground of delay.

The Supreme Court in the case of Skoda Auto Volkswagen (India) Private Limited. Vs. State of U.P. and others, reported in (2021) 5 SCC 795 has held that mere delay on the part of complainant in lodging the complaint, cannot by itself be a ground to quash the FIR.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Court cannot embark upon an enquiry to find out the reliability or genuineness of allegations made in FIR or in complaint and criminal proceedings can not be scuttled at the initial stage.
21. No other argument was advanced by counsel for applicants.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:10924 22.
Considering the totality of facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of considered opinion that no case is made out warranting interference.

23. Accordingly, M.Cr.C. No.36013 of 2023 filed by Bharat Kumar Choudhary (father-in-law), Smt.
Suneeta Choudhary (mother-in-law), Nishant Choudhary (younger brother-in-law) and Ku. Kamini Choudhary (sister-in-law) is also hereby dismissed.
